issue.title: Range-partitioned JoinScan converts sampled NUMERIC partition bounds twice

relevant_locations.role: Applies numeric scaling and byte conversion to range bounds
Defines fast field requests used to fetch stored column values

llm_context.input_title: Range-partitioned JoinScan converts sampled NUMERIC partition bounds twice
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: Range-partitioned JoinScan samples `partition_by` fast fields in their raw/stored form, but then wraps these split points in normal `pdb::Query::Range` filters. Because `pdb::Query::Range` automatically runs `scale_numeric_bound` on `Numeric64` fields and parses `NumericBytes` bounds, sampled numeric partition bounds get converted twice or trigger conversion errors.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: The root cause is a mismatch between how user-provided query bounds and sampled partition bounds are processed. `pdb::Query::Range` assumes input bounds are logical user inputs that require scaling (`scale_numeric_bound`) or byte-conversion (`numeric_bound_to_bytes`). However, range-partitioned join scans supply already-stored internal fast field values, leading to duplicate scaling for `Numeric64` and invalid type conversion errors for `NumericBytes`.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect pdb::Query::Range handling
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect the range query construction and execution logic in pg_search/src/query/pdb_query.rs to understand how scale_numeric_bound and numeric_bound_to_bytes are applied.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect sample_fast_field and WhichFastField usage
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine how WhichFastField and sample_fast_field extract raw/stored partition bounds in pg_search/src/index/fast_fields_helper.rs.

step_by_step_plan.title: Prevent double scaling or conversion for sampled bounds
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the range query constructor or introduce a dedicated variant/flag in pg_search/src/query/pdb_query.rs so that sampled numeric or byte partition bounds bypass redundant scaling and byte conversion.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add regression test and verify with cargo test
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a regression test case covering range-partitioned join scans on Numeric64 and NumericBytes columns, then execute the verified test command to ensure correctness.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: A technique where decimals are stored as scaled integers (e.g., multiplying by 10^scale) to avoid floating-point inaccuracies.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Developers must ensure scaling is applied exactly once during round-tripping to prevent data corruption or skewed partitions.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Sampled `Numeric64` bounds are already stored in their scaled form, but passing them through `range()` applies scaling a second time.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The mechanism that translates high-level search range bounds (inclusive/exclusive/unbounded) into low-level query terms.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Query filters must accurately interpret boundaries to return correct search results without runtime type errors.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: `NumericBytes` range bounds expect sortable byte representations, but raw sampled bytes fail validation when treated as unencoded inputs.

common_pitfalls: Modifying global numeric scaling functions without checking how standard user queries vs. internal partition scans construct their ranges.
Forgetting to update DataFusion range partitioning declarations (`RangePartitioning::to_datafusion`) when changing how partition bounds are interpreted.
